findings.text: the assertion compares the waiver reason the test itself passed in with the stored row's echo of it, so it holds for any implementation that records the caller's string and cannot distinguish a recorded waiver from an echoed input; it is weak rather than vacuous, since a path that dropped the waiver fails the lookup, and the file's refusal half at lines 244-252 does not depend on it.

the promotion's waiver assertion has the same shape as the one above -- the literal the test handed complete() on one side, its echo on the other -- with the same failure condition; the file's four guard assertions (lines 213-219, 230-233, 248-254, 269-274) are outcome assertions and do not rest on it.

justifications.durability: restoring the terminal-manifest-only admission in a scratch copy of the reviewed head reddens three of the four cases -- the resumed case and the no-manifest case with DID NOT RAISE, the stale-manifest case on the absence of the refusal (3 failed, 1 passed in 28.30s, EXIT=1) -- so the guard is non-vacuous and the cases are its guards, while the file's precondition assertions read the code's own helpers and the waiver round-trips cannot distinguish a recorded waiver from an echoed input.
justifications.evidence: the gate's figures reconcile with logs/base-suite.log and logs/head-suite.log (identical 69-file populations, identical 15-id failure sets, EXIT=1 each) and the added-failure count derives to 0, but the reviewed head is 9acd66c41 while the recorded head arm ran 4467cf004, which I could only accept because the tail commit is docs-only, and the population had to be rebuilt three times across reviews before it reached the 69 files the fence's import-based list could not see.
justifications.fit: the guard's local import of recovery inside the function (reckon/crew/promotion.py:3430) matches the module's existing idiom for cross-module reads, the new refusal message keeps the surrounding phrasing, both new test files are ruff-clean and promotion.py's three findings are unchanged from base, and the added names and docstrings carry no plan, sprint or ticket identifier.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/promotion.py:3431 refuses the resumed shape (a live attempt with no manifest of its own), which I reproduced green at the reviewed head and red against a mutated copy of it; the superseded arm at promotion.py:3436 can only fire where a fresh terminal manifest predates the launch, so for a real resume the refusal is the manifest-is-None clause rather than the arm the docstring frames as the resume case, which is correct in behaviour and imprecise only in which branch is credited.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff is inside the declared scope once the coordinator's three recorded widenings are read, and the edits to the previously-green fixtures are waiver arguments with no assertion changed (tests/test_ledger.py:222-228, tests/test_crew.py:1958-1964), though the diff does reverse a contract asserted by tests/test_complete_refuses_a_live_run.py:233, which the coordinator decided explicitly in resume-4 rather than the worker choosing it.
